abstract: Accurate characterization of CRISPR knock-in requires distinguishing site-specific integration from total donor abundance and donor-derived background while measuring editing at the target site. Here, we present CRISPR-dPCR, a modular multiplex digital PCR framework combining a locked nucleic acid-enhanced cut-site assay with junction-based detection and two orthogonal short-amplicon strategies: Poisson linkage and homology-arm subtraction. We evaluated assay modules across genomic loci, neuroblastoma models and primary human T cells, with selected assays compared on two dPCR platforms. In genotype-defined clones and mixtures with low residual donor, homology-arm subtraction most closely recovered expected knock-in abundance. Linkage provided highly specific evidence of target-cargo association without junction-spanning amplification, whereas junction assays supplied boundary-specific confirmation but were more sensitive to amplicon length and multiplexing. Five-channel panels integrated cut-site editing, donor abundance, copy-number normalization and site-specific knock-in in a single reaction. Residual donor DNA limited quantitative interpretation, particularly in early post-editing samples. Modular extensions quantified defined unintended outcomes, including chromosomal translocations. CRISPR-dPCR integrates complementary measurements into a scalable analytical framework for genome-editing research, cell and gene therapy product development and applications in longitudinal clinical monitoring of targeted integration and transgene persistence.
